text:
॥ Om, the imperishable, the support of the end of the body (the body’s ultimate limit). ॥ 1/3/10 ॥

The qualities such as invisibility have been declared to belong to Vishnu. [This is so] because of the statement “the unseen, the seer, the heard, the hearer,” and so on, and because of the possibility of the middle syllable [of Om] being declared [to refer to Vishnu] from statements such as “I, Soma, sustain the day and the night.” Therefore, [the text] states: “The imperishable is the support of the end of the body.”

The imperishable is Brahman, which is the support of the entire end of the body, as stated in the Śruti: “In this imperishable, O Gārgya, is woven and unwoven [the fabric of existence].” This is also supported by the Śruti: “Who, being the threefold element, sustains the earth, the sky, and all the worlds alone?”; “Being the sustainer, He is sustained; the one God abides in many forms, sustaining all.”; “In whom this [universe] is woven together and apart, in whom all the gods are seated.”

And as stated in the Skanda Purāṇa: “Whatever is past, present, and future, from the earth up to the end of Prakṛti, Vishnu alone sustains this; there is none other than Him, for He is the support of all that is sustained.”
